description: Intent i014 (SNAPSHOT=s04, BRANCH=loop-parser-stale-state) complete. Credible variant found: net/802/garp.c garp_pdu_parse_attr() (lines 447-488, reported with high confidence) is a same-function structural duplicate of the seed's pep_get_sb() bug. Evidence: untrusted GARP/MRP attribute headers parsed in the per-attribute loop of garp_pdu_parse_msg (net/802/garp.c:503-508, entered from garp_pdu_rcv via stp_proto_register); ga = (struct garp_attr_hdr *)skb->data captured at line 449; pskb_may_pull(skb, ga->len) at line 453 with the pull length taken from the attacker-controlled header (exactly like pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len)); then stale ga dereferenced post-pull at line 456 (ga->len), line 461 (ga->event switch), and line 485 (ga->data passed to garp_attr_lookup with attacker dlen) with no refetch — pskb_may_pull may __pskb_pull_tail/pskb_expand_head the skb head, making ga a use-after-free read that gates GARP state transitions. Candidates classified: x25_decode (net/x25/x25_subr.c:296) safe — refetches frame=skb->data after every pull; batadv_bla_process_claim (net/batman-adv/bridge_loop_avoidance.c:1138) safe — explicit refetch of ethhdr after pskb_may_pull with comment; nci_hci_data_received_cb (net/nfc/nci/hci.c:496) and nfc_hci_recv_shdl_chain (net/nfc/hci/core.c:917) safe — refetch packet pointer after pskb_may_pull; pep.c pep_get_sb left unresolved as the seed location itself (assigned to i012). Bounded negative evidence: custom static analysis (find_stale.py, $TMPDIR/i014) over all of net/ plus drivers/net produced 66 same-function capture->pull->use candidates; the two loop-context ones and all high-signal remaining ones were triaged and only garp_pdu_parse_attr lacks a refetch. Limitations: heuristic static scan (no runtime non-linearity proof, no cross-function pointer-return tracking), drivers/ outside drivers/net not deeply scanned, and no reproducer was built — finding is a hypothesis with untrusted source, violated invariant (pointer into skb head alive across head-reallocating pull with untrusted length), and unsafe use confirmed by exact source evidence.
